newsitem.title: GERMANY: French strike hits VW hardest in German car sector.
newsitem.headline: French strike hits VW hardest in German car sector.

text.p: Only Volkswagen AG among Germany's major car makers faced production cut-backs as a truckers' strike choked highways in France, company spokesmen said on Wednesday.
Volkswagen, Europe's largest car maker, warned that the strike could disrupt its parts supplies, forcing it to decide next Monday whether to introduce short-time working at its main Wolfsburg plant.
VW imports heating and air conditioning systems for its Golf and Polo models from plants in central France and gets metal parts for the Polo from Spain.
Striking French truckers have set up almost 200 truck blockades on major routes and blocked refineries and fuel depots around France, forcing some factories to close.
Aside from VW, German car makers said the strikes were having little impact on their schedules.
"We do not have any reports of deliveries from France being a problem," a spokesman at Mercedes-Benz AG said.
The spokesman also said that a Mercedes truck plant in Woerth, that receives a large number of parts from France, had so far had no production problems.

A spokesman for Bayerische Motoren Werke AG (BMW) also said the company did not face any production cut-backs now. "There will not be any difficulties this week, but it could be tight in the coming weeks," he said.
A spokesman for Opel AG, a unit of General Motors Corp, said production at its major plants had not been disrupted.
Opel said that deliveries of French parts for its Corsa model had been delayed only slightly, but that production had not been slowed.
